newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN IPOs - Sharp fall in August mobilisation.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN IPOs - Sharp fall in August mobilisation.

text.p: The total mobilisation through public issues in August fell to only 3,630 million rupees, much lower than 16,750 million rupees in July, Prime Database said.
Prithvi Haldea of Prime, the country's leading database on the primary capital market, said there were no debt issues in August.

The number of issues remained at a high level with as many as 87 companies tapping the market in August. This was, however, lower than 99 issues in July and 127 issues during June. In the earlier months, there were 73 issues in May and 105 in April.
Mobilisation in May was 6,750 million rupees and 3,780 million rupees in April, Prime said.

However, according to Prime, the response to the issues continued to remain extremely poor. Of the issues which opened in the earlier half of August, several had to stay open till the last closing dates.

Among these were the issues of Indian Lead, Prakash Paper, Marvel Industries, Mardia Copper, D.S. Bagrecha Lease, Kinetic Copper, Rasdhara Agro, Krishna Mingranite, Peony Investments, RGF Capital Market, Ramchandra Leasing, Suku Jain Associates, Money Television, Rajgarh Investments and Parque Foods. Other issues too evoked poor response from the investors.

Suggesting poor market sentiment was also the fact that only five of the 87 issues of the month were underwritten. These were the issues of Exim Finance, Aramusk Developers, Monnet Industries, Kothari Petrochemicals and Super Auto Forge. The first four had no provision for an earliest closing date.
Compared to three in May, ten in June and five in July, August had 5 issues of 100 million rupees plus, Prime said.

These were from Apcotex (172.50 million rupees), Mukand Engineers (120.30 million rupees), Money Television (120 million rupees), Monnet Industries (113.10 million rupees) and Marvel Industries (108 million rupees).

Prime said the market in August was again deluged with a large number of small issues; 40 of the 87 issues (46 percent) were below 30 million rupees, of which one was even less than 10 million rupees.

Worse, unlike the previous four months, the dominance of issues from finance companies re-emerged, Prime said. As many as 35 of the 87 issues (40 percent) were from this sector, unlike 26 to 29 percent in April-July period.
During the month, the issues of Bell South Enterprises, Hindustan Maize Products and Bhoruka Engineering had to be withdrawn on the eve of the opening of subscription list.
This has brought to 18 the total of issues which have been cancelled/withdrawn since April literally at the last moment, Prime said.

According to Haldea, premia issues continued to remain out of sight in August too. Only 11 of the 87 issues in August (8 out of 99 in July) were offered at a premium, with the only high premia issues being from Apcotex (105 rupees) and Super Auto Forge (70 rupees).
Subsequent to the April 1996 guidelines of SEBI, there continues to be a significant slowdown in the number of new issue documents being submitted for vetting.

A total of 143 documents had been filed in February, which rose to 221 in March and further to 392 in April. This, however, fell to only 90 in May, 51 in June, 49 in July and on to 43 in August upto the 24th August, Prime said.
The debt issues are expected to resurface from September onwards, Haldea said.

Some of the forthcoming debt issues include IDBI (10 billion rupees), Larsen & Toubro (5 billion rupees), TISCO (5 billion rupees), Arvind Mills (1 billion rupees) and Kotak Mahindra Finance (1 billion rupees).
